recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-34142 unless a future work-group decision changes the warning severity or the orderMeaning/slicing rule.
issue_request: FHIR-34142 is a Published FHIR-core/FHIR-I change request with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It requested a warning invariant on ElementDefinition so that, when orderMeaning is absent, slicing.rules=openAtEnd or slicing.ordered=true is warned against because order-dependent slicing is improper where element order has no meaning.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied directly by git commit bfba74805d, which added invariant 25 to source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml with warning severity, the requested human message, and the requested FHIRPath/XPath logic. The R5 history artifacts also carry the generated eld-25 warning.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes ElementDefinition in the [types] list, marks it normative, and maps it to the eld prefix, so the spreadsheet row is in the current build scope for the ElementDefinition datatype. Broader Jira searching found FHIR-13461 as an older, broader openAtEnd/orderMeaning warning request, but that issue was retracted and Resolved - No Change before FHIR-34142 was resolved. Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant community evidence that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already implements the requested warning invariant for missing orderMeaning with openAtEnd or ordered slicing, including the requested message, FHIRPath, and XPath.

related_jiras.note: Older broader request for slice-rule warnings involving openAtEnd and orderMeaning; it was retracted and does not override the later applied FHIR-34142 decision.
